reproduction_target: A population-genomics study of sunflower (Helianthus annuus) domestication and improvement, with one small wet-lab/phenotyping component. The computational reproduction target is the chain that turns published resequencing reads into selection and load statistics and then links them to a salt-tolerance phenotype: (1) fastp trimming, Bowtie2 alignment to HanXRQr2.0-SUNRISE, Picard duplicate removal and GATK HaplotypeCaller SNP calling with explicit hard filters, over 332 accessions taken from Huebner et al. 2019, yielding 11.3 million SNPs; (2) PLINK PCA and an IBS-derived (1 - IBS) neighbour-joining tree built with the R ape package and drawn with ggtree; (3) an XP-CLR positive-selection scan (landrace vs wild, modern vs landrace) and a BalLeRMix balancing-selection scan, with top-1% outlier sweep calling and merging of adjacent sweeps; (4) zero-shot deleteriousness scoring of all 11.3 M SNPs with the Plant Caduceus DNA language model, classification into top-1/5/10% deleterious sets, and a 1,000-permutation enrichment test of deleterious SNPs inside selected regions; (5) GEMMA mixed-model GWAS (Q from PLINK PCs, K from TASSEL 5.0) on salt-responsive germination-ratio and radicle-length traits measured in an independent 274-accession panel, with a PLINK indep-pairwise-derived significance threshold and ancestral-allele effect estimation from GEMMA betas. The single wet-lab component is the petri-dish salt-germination assay (200 mM NaCl vs water, 27 C, four days, three replicates) that produces the GWAS phenotypes.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool-invocation, built from the bioRxiv v1 JATS source XML (fetched with curl and a browser User-Agent; WebFetch returned HTTP 403 on the JATS URL). The Methods are a single 'Materials and Methods' section with six subsections; all computational sentences were mined from them. The declared artifact is one GitHub repository (https://github.com/GenXu1/Sunflower_domestication), whose landing page and README prose were read; the README is 12 lines and describes only two top-level directories ('01table': supplementary tables; '02codes': 'the code and scripts to generate the figures and results'). No workflow source was read (Stage 2 scope). The repository's visible code tree covers Fig1, Fig2 and Fig4 only (directories 01Fig1, 02Fig2, 04Fig4); there is no directory corresponding to Fig3 (deleterious load) and none corresponding to the upstream variant-calling pipeline, but at Stage 1 this is recorded as landing-page observation, not as a verified code-coverage claim. One wet-lab step (the salt-germination assay) is recorded as layer W / OOS and excluded from S.
capture_claim_note: The paper pins exact version strings for seven tools (fastp version 0.20.0; Bowtie2 version 2.4.4; Picard tools version 2.18; GATK version 4.1; BalLeRMix version 2.3; R v4.3.0; TASSEL 5.0) and names the reference genome build (HanXRQr2.0-SUNRISE). It leaves the rest floating: XP-CLR is cited as 'the latest version of the cross-population composite likelihood ratio (XP-CLR)', which is an explicitly moving target; GEMMA, Plant Caduceus (no model checkpoint or weights identifier), the ape and ggtree R packages, and the custom sweep-merging / permutation scripts carry no version at all; 'plink1.9' names a release line spanning many builds, not a build. No environment closure of any kind is claimed anywhere in the paper or the README: no container, no digest, no conda environment.yml, no renv.lock or requirements file, no Python version, no compute-platform statement. The GitHub repository has zero releases and zero tags, so 'release_snapshot' was considered and rejected. Under protocol v0.2.6 exact_pins_partial is NOT on the positive Stage-2 gate (Delta-2 caps version at 1 from the prose read, so a code check yields no R-star gain), hence stage2_candidate=false; this paper can only reach Stage 2 through the orchestrator's stratified audit draw.

steps.label: Read trimming with fastp version 0.20.0 - verbatim: 'We then processed raw sequencing reads with fastp (version 0.20.0) to trim adapter sequences and remove low-quality bases before downstream analyses'. Version pinned; no options given (no adapter sequence, no quality or length cutoff, no dedup flag), so defaults are implied but not declared. Input is the 332-accession read set 'from a previous study (Huebner et al., 2019)', for which this paper gives no accession number and no per-accession run identifiers - only Table S1 is cited for the sample list

Alignment to the reference genome with Bowtie2 version 2.4.4 - verbatim: 'the cleaned reads were aligned to the reference genome HanXRQr2.0-SUNRISE (Badouin et al., 2017) using Bowtie2 (version 2.4.4)'. Tool version and reference-genome build name are both given; no Bowtie2 options (preset, --maxins, --no-mixed etc.) and no download source or checksum for the HanXRQr2.0-SUNRISE FASTA are given

Duplicate removal with Picard tools version 2.18 - verbatim: 'we removed the duplicated reads using Picard tools (version 2.18)'. Version pinned; the Picard sub-command (MarkDuplicates) is not named and no options (REMOVE_DUPLICATES, OPTICAL_DUPLICATE_PIXEL_DISTANCE, VALIDATION_STRINGENCY) are given

SNP calling and hard filtering with GATK version 4.1 HaplotypeCaller - verbatim: 'conducted SNP calling using Genome Analysis Toolkit's (GATK, version 4.1) HaplotypeCaller (McKenna et al., 2010), with the following parameters: QD < 2.0, FS > 60.0, MQ < 20.0, MQRankSum < -12.5, and ReadPosRankSum < -8.0, to filter out low-quality SNPs'. Version pinned and the complete hard-filter expression is given; the intermediate steps (GVCF mode, GenomicsDBImport/CombineGVCFs, GenotypeGVCFs, SelectVariants) and the ploidy/interval settings are not described, and the resulting 11.3 M-SNP VCF is not deposited anywhere

Missingness filtering of the SNP set - verbatim: 'In addition, we removed SNPs with missing rates > 50%'. The threshold is explicit, but no tool is named for this step (VCFtools, bcftools, PLINK are all plausible) and no minor-allele-frequency or biallelic filter is stated even though the downstream count of 11.3 million SNPs depends on the full filter chain

Principal component analysis with PLINK - verbatim: 'We performed PCA using SNP dataset with plink1.9 (Chang et al., 2015)'. No sub-command (--pca), no number of components, no LD-pruning or MAF pre-filter, and no random seed are given; 'plink1.9' is the tool's release line, not a build identifier (PLINK 1.9 ships as 1.90bNN with differing behaviour across betas). The three PCs later used as the GWAS Q matrix come from this step, so the ambiguity propagates

IBS distance matrix and neighbour-joining tree - verbatim: 'we computed identity-by-state (IBS) values among the 332 sunflower accessions with the parameter "-ibs-matrix". The resulting IBS similarity matrix was converted into a genetic distance matrix (1 - IBS), which was then used to construct a neighbor-joining (NJ) phylogenetic tree using the ape package (Paradis and Schliep, 2019) in R (v4.3.0). The tree was visualized with a circular layout using the "ggtree" package'. The PLINK flag, the distance transform and the tree method are all explicit; but the R runtime is the only versioned component (v4.3.0) - neither ape nor ggtree carries a package version, and no renv/sessionInfo record is offered, so the R-package layer is unpinned

Positive-selection scan with XP-CLR - verbatim: 'We performed a genome-wide scan for positive selection signals using the latest version of the cross-population composite likelihood ratio (XP-CLR) (Chen et al., 2010). In the XP-CLR analysis, we used a 50 kb sliding window and a 5 kb step size. To ensure comparability of the composite likelihood score in each window, we fixed the number assayed in each window to 100 SNPs.' Window, step and per-window SNP count are given, but 'the latest version' is an explicitly floating version claim - it names no release, no commit and no implementation (the original C implementation and the widely used Python reimplementation differ), and neither the recombination-map/grid-size setting nor the two population contrasts' sample lists are specified here

Balancing-selection scan with BalLeRMix version 2.3 - verbatim: 'We then conducted a balancing selection scan with default parameters using BalLeRMix (version 2.3) (Cheng and DeGiorgio, 2020). Using the major alleles in wild species as ancestral alleles, we calculated the derived allele frequency (DAF).' Version pinned and 'default parameters' is an explicit (if coarse) parameter declaration; the B-statistic variant (B0/B1/B2 - the Results and Table S2 refer to 'B2 loci') is not stated in the Methods text, and no spectrum file or window specification is described

Sweep definition and merging - verbatim: 'For both positive and balancing selection, we considered the 1% outliers as the selective sweeps; adjacent sweeps separated by a physical distance of < 50 kb were merged into a single selected sweep.' The rule is fully stated numerically, and downstream counts depend on it (652 domestication and 549 improvement sweeps; 67 Mb and 56.9 Mb). No tool, script name or version is named for the outlier-calling and merging operation, and the gene-annotation source used to assign the 1,919 / 2,062 genes to sweeps is not identified

Deleteriousness scoring of 11.3 M SNPs with the Plant Caduceus DNA language model - verbatim: 'We used Plant Caduceus (Zhai et al., 2025), a DNA language model that infers the relative fitness effects of nucleotide substitutions through a zero-shot comparison of reference and alternate allele probabilities, to compute site-specific zero-shot scores (ZSS) ... Variants were then classified into the top 1%, 5%, and 10% most deleterious categories based on their ZSS distributions'. The classification thresholds are explicit, but the model itself is entirely unpinned: no checkpoint name or size (PlantCaduceus ships in several parameter scales), no weights DOI or HuggingFace revision, no context-window length, no batch/precision settings, and no PyTorch or CUDA version. This is the step generating Figure 3, one of the paper's four headline results

Permutation enrichment test of deleterious SNPs inside selected regions - verbatim: 'we calculated the observed number of deleterious SNPs within selected regions and compared it with a null distribution generated from 1,000 sets of randomly sampled genomic windows matched in size'. The permutation count and the size-matching criterion are stated; no tool, script, random seed or test statistic definition is given, and 'matched in size' does not say whether SNP density, mappability or chromosome were also matched - which determines whether the reported significance (P <= 0.01) is reproducible

Mixed-model GWAS with GEMMA on salt-responsive traits - verbatim: 'We performed a genome-wide association analysis (GWAS) for salt responsiveness of germination ratio and radicle length using GEMMA (Zhou and Stephens, 2012), based on 226,779 high-quality SNPs generated in our previous study (Delen et al., 2024). We applied a mixed model Q + K ... The Q matrix consisted of the first three principal components calculated using plink1.9, while the K matrix was estimated with TASSEL 5.0'. The model specification is complete and TASSEL is version-labelled, but GEMMA carries no version and no invocation flags (-lmm 1/2/4 changes the reported test), and the phenotype inputs - the germination-ratio and radicle-length measurements produced by this study's own salt assay on 274 accessions - are not deposited in any archive or named supplementary table, so the step's primary input is absent

Independent-marker estimation and significance-threshold derivation with PLINK - verbatim: 'we used a genome-wide threshold of 2.9 x 10-5, corresponding to 1/n, where n = 33,801 represents the number of independent SNPs. The number of independent markers was estimated using PLINK's "indep-pairwise" function (window size = 10 kb, step size = 10, r2 >= 0.1). The significant GWAS loci were then defined by extending 50 kb upstream and downstream of each significant SNP, and the overlapping windows were merged into single genomic intervals.' All three pruning parameters, the threshold arithmetic and the locus-definition rule are explicit; the PLINK build is again only 'plink1.9' (release line, not build) and the merging is done by an unnamed script

Ancestral-allele effect estimation - verbatim: 'We estimated the sizes of allele effects using the beta coefficients from the GEMMA output. To determine the ancestral allele, we assigned the allele with the highest frequency in the wild group as the ancestral allele. A positive effect of the ancestral allele indicates that the ancestral allele contributes to a higher phenotypic value than the derived allele.' The polarisation rule and the effect-size source are stated, and this step produces Figure 4B and the paper's central breeding claim. But it joins two panels that are never explicitly reconciled - the 332-accession resequencing panel (which defines the wild group and hence the ancestral allele) and the 274-accession association panel (which supplies the GEMMA betas) - and no script, version or accession-mapping table is given for that join; the phenotype side of the input is again undeposited

Salt-tolerance assay at the seedling stage on an independent 274-accession panel - verbatim: 'we treated seeds with a fungicide and placed them in petri dishes. Under control conditions, we germinated the seeds in pure water, whereas under salt treatment, we germinated them in a 200 mM NaCl solution. We maintained all petri dishes in a 27 degrees C growth chamber for four days. After incubation, we recorded the germination ratio and radicle length for each accession, using three biological replicates per treatment.' Accessions come from USDA-ARS NCRPIS (Ames, Iowa). The fungicide is unnamed and the number of seeds per dish is not stated. Wet-lab layer, OOS, excluded from S

headline.static_readiness: 0/15 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI on 5/15 computational steps (C1 fastp, C2 Bowtie2, C3 Picard, C4 GATK HaplotypeCaller, C9 BalLeRMix), NI on 9/15 (C5 missingness filter, C7 IBS/NJ tree, C8 XP-CLR, C10 sweep calling, C11 Plant Caduceus, C12 permutation test, C13 GEMMA GWAS, C14 PLINK pruning, C15 ancestral-allele effects), X on 1/15 (C6 PLINK PCA). The distribution is unusually informative: the five RI steps are exactly the five standard upstream read-processing tools, every one of which the paper version-pins; every step downstream of the VCF loses the version axis. Three distinct causes account for that. (1) Explicitly floating versions: XP-CLR is used at 'the latest version', which cannot be re-instantiated at any later date. (2) Unpinned model and library layers: Plant Caduceus - the tool behind the entire deleterious-load result in Figure 3 - is named with no checkpoint, weights revision, scale or runtime; ape and ggtree carry no package versions even though the R runtime v4.3.0 is given; GEMMA carries no version at all. (3) Unnamed in-house scripts: the missingness filter, the top-1%-outlier sweep caller and 50 kb merger, the 1,000-permutation enrichment test and the two-panel ancestral-allele join are all custom operations with numerically explicit rules but no code identity in the prose. The parameter axis, by contrast, is this paper's strength - 10 of 15 steps score params=2 because the authors state numeric thresholds (GATK hard filters, XP-CLR 50 kb/5 kb/100 SNPs, top-1% and 50 kb merging, 1,000 permutations, indep-pairwise 10 kb/10/0.1, threshold 2.9e-5, +/-50 kb locus extension) rather than gesturing at 'default settings'. Two axis-zero facts limit the ceiling independently of code: no sequence accession is given anywhere (the 332-accession read set is attributed only to 'a previous study (Huebner et al., 2019)'), and the salt-assay phenotypes that drive the GWAS (C13, C15) are not deposited in any archive.
headline.coverage: 15 computational steps and 1 wet-lab step assessed from the bioRxiv v1 JATS Methods prose plus the GitHub landing page and README prose. This is a mixed paper that is overwhelmingly computational in weight - the single wet-lab step is a four-day petri-dish germination assay whose only role is to supply GWAS phenotypes - so the OOS layer removes almost nothing from the reproduction target. The README was readable (12 lines, HTTP 200) but contains no methods content: it restates the abstract and lists two directories. No install instructions, no dependency list, no environment file, no figure-to-script map, no data-download step.

gaps.where: Data availability statement; inputs to C1-C4 and to the 11.3 M-SNP set used by C5-C12
gaps.missing: No sequence accession appears anywhere in the paper. The Data Availability statement reads in full: 'Supplementary data and code are available on the GitHub repository: https://github.com/GenXu1/Sunflower_domestication.' It covers code and tables only. The primary input is described solely as 'We downloaded raw sequence data from 332 sunflower accessions, including modern cultivars (n = 288), landraces (n = 18), and wild relatives (n = 26), from a previous study (Huebner et al., 2019)' - a citation, not an SRA/ENA BioProject accession, and with no per-accession run identifiers in the prose. Table S1 is cited for the sample list, but the URL the paper gives for it is dead (see the type-6 gap below).
gaps.how_to_close: State the SRA/ENA BioProject and per-accession run accessions for the 332 resequencing samples, and provide a machine-readable accession-to-group (wild/landrace/modern) mapping table in the repository.

gaps.missing: The germination-ratio and radicle-length measurements produced by this study's own salt assay on 274 accessions, and the derived salt-responsive (SR) trait values, are not deposited anywhere. The paper states the assay protocol and the SR formula but names no supplementary table, archive or repository file holding the per-accession phenotype values. The 226,779 genotype SNPs are likewise attributed only to 'our previous study (Delen et al., 2024)' with no accession. Table S6 in the repository holds GWAS output, not the phenotype input.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the per-accession, per-replicate germination-ratio and radicle-length values (control and 200 mM NaCl) plus the computed SR traits as a supplementary table or archive record, and give the accession for the 226,779-SNP genotype matrix.

gaps.where: Whole analysis environment (C1-C15); GitHub repository root
gaps.missing: No environment closure of any kind is claimed in the paper or the README. The repository root contains only .DS_Store, .gitignore, 01table/, 02codes/, LICENSE, README.md and Sunflower_domestication.Rproj - there is no environment.yml, no conda-lock, no renv.lock, no requirements.txt, no Dockerfile or image digest, no sessionInfo dump, and no Python or CUDA version statement (relevant because C11 runs a DNA language model). The .Rproj file records an RStudio project, not a dependency set. Version pinning stops at individual tool version strings for seven of the tools, which is exact_pins_partial, not a lock.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a conda-lock or container digest covering the fastp/Bowtie2/Picard/GATK/PLINK/XP-CLR/BalLeRMix/GEMMA/TASSEL stack, an renv.lock for the R side (ape, ggtree), and a pinned Python/PyTorch environment plus the Plant Caduceus checkpoint identifier for the deleteriousness scoring; declare the platform each was resolved for.

gaps.missing: The model that produces the paper's entire deleterious-load result (Figure 3, and the enrichment claims in C12) is unpinned. Verbatim: 'We used Plant Caduceus (Zhai et al., 2025), a DNA language model ... to compute site-specific zero-shot scores (ZSS)'. No checkpoint name, no parameter scale (the released PlantCaduceus family spans several sizes with different scores), no weights DOI or HuggingFace revision hash, no context window, no precision or batch setting, and no inference-code version. Zero-shot scores are not comparable across checkpoints, so the 1%/5%/10% cutoffs are not re-derivable.
gaps.how_to_close: Name the exact PlantCaduceus checkpoint and revision (repository plus commit or model hash), the context length and precision used, and deposit the per-SNP ZSS table so the thresholds can be re-derived independently of model access.

gaps.missing: Verbatim: 'using the latest version of the cross-population composite likelihood ratio (XP-CLR) (Chen et al., 2010)'. 'Latest version' is a self-invalidating version claim: it names no release, tag or commit, and does not identify which implementation was used (the original Chen et al. C program and the widely used Python reimplementation differ in scoring and in how the per-window SNP cap is applied). The recombination map or genetic-distance input, which XP-CLR requires, is not mentioned at all.
gaps.how_to_close: Name the XP-CLR implementation with a repository URL and commit hash, state the version used, and specify the genetic map (or the constant recombination rate) supplied to it.

gaps.missing: Version identity stops short of the packages that actually compute results. R is pinned at v4.3.0 but neither ape nor ggtree carries a package version; GEMMA is cited with no version; PLINK is written as 'plink1.9', which designates a release line whose betas (1.90b3 through 1.90b7) differ in --indep-pairwise and --pca behaviour, not a build. TASSEL 5.0 is likewise a major line rather than a build.
gaps.how_to_close: Record the exact package and binary versions (sessionInfo() for the R side; --version output for PLINK, GEMMA and TASSEL) in the repository alongside the scripts.

gaps.where: Code availability / repository contents (C1-C5, C11, C12)
gaps.missing: The repository is public and readable, but its README describes 02codes only as 'the code and scripts to generate the figures and results', and the visible code tree contains three directories - 01Fig1, 02Fig2, 04Fig4. There is no directory for Figure 3 (the deleterious-load analysis) and nothing corresponding to the upstream variant-calling pipeline (C1-C5) or to the permutation test (C12). At Stage 1 this is a landing-page observation rather than a verified coverage claim, but the README makes no statement about which analyses are and are not included, and the repository has no release, no tag and no citation file. The paper's Data Availability statement conflates code and supplementary data in one sentence and gives no commit or DOI, so there is no way to cite the state of the code at submission.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a README section mapping every Methods step to a script path (and stating explicitly which steps are not included), mint a DOI-bearing archival snapshot (Zenodo/Software Heritage) of the commit used for the paper, and cite that DOI in the Data/Code Availability statement.

gaps.where: Supporting Information - all six supplementary table URLs
gaps.missing: Every supplementary-table link printed in the paper is dead. The paper cites, for example, 'Table S1. List of accessions included in the analyses. (https://github.com/GenXu1/Sunflower_domestication/tree/main/02table/TableS1_sample_info.xlsx)' and five analogous URLs under 02table/. The repository has no 02table directory - the tables live in 01table/ under different names ('Supplementary Table S1.xlsx' ... 'Supplementary Table S7.xlsx'), and a live check of the cited TableS1 URL returned HTTP 404. Two consequences are load-bearing: the sample list (Table S1) is the only stated route to the identity of the 332 accessions, and the file names differ enough that the mapping is not one-to-one (the repository holds seven tables where the paper cites six; the paper's Table S6 is titled 'GWAS results' but points at a file named TableS6_positive_selection_loci.xlsx, while the repository additionally carries a stale-lock artefact named ~$TableS5_Salt_GWAS.xlsx). Which repository file corresponds to which cited table cannot be settled from prose.
gaps.how_to_close: Repair the six URLs to point at the current 01table/ paths, keep the file names identical to the table numbers used in the text, remove the stray ~$ Excel lock files, and state the commit or release the links refer to.

gaps.missing: Four steps name a tool - three of them version-pinned - but give no invocation parameters. fastp: no adapter sequence, quality cutoff, minimum length or dedup setting. Bowtie2: no preset (--very-sensitive vs default), no insert-size bounds, no --no-mixed/--no-discordant choice. Picard: no sub-command named and no MarkDuplicates options. PLINK PCA: no --pca flag, no component count, no LD-pruning or MAF pre-filter and no seed. Defaults may have been used throughout, but that is not stated, and for Bowtie2 the preset choice materially changes the SNP set entering every downstream step.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the full command lines for the read-processing and PCA steps, or state explicitly that default settings were used for each named tool.

gaps.where: C15 - the join between the 332-accession resequencing panel and the 274-accession association panel
gaps.missing: The paper's central claim - that ancestral alleles inside positively selected sweeps tend to enhance salt tolerance - requires combining two different panels: ancestral alleles are polarised using the wild group of the 332-accession resequencing set, while the effect sizes come from GEMMA run on the separate 274-accession NCRPIS panel genotyped with 226,779 SNPs. The Methods never state how SNPs are matched across the two panels (coordinate liftover is not needed if both use HanXRQr2.0, but the paper does not say the Delen et al. 2024 genotypes are on that build), how strand or allele coding is reconciled, or what is done when a GWAS SNP is absent from the resequencing set. Figure 4B additionally reports SR values 'across wild (WD), landrace (LR), and modern (MD) accessions', implying a group assignment for the association panel that is never described.
gaps.how_to_close: State the reference build of the 226,779-SNP genotype set, describe the SNP-matching and allele-polarisation procedure between the two panels explicitly, and publish the group assignment used for the association panel in Figure 4B.

gaps.missing: Verbatim: 'compared it with a null distribution generated from 1,000 sets of randomly sampled genomic windows matched in size'. Matching is stated for size only. Whether the random windows were also matched for SNP density, gene content, chromosome or mappability is not stated - and because deleterious SNP counts scale with SNP density, an unmatched null inflates the enrichment. No random seed is given, so the reported P <= 0.01 cannot be reproduced exactly.
gaps.how_to_close: Specify every matching covariate used to draw the null windows, publish the sampling script with its random seed, and report the observed and null counts numerically rather than only as a violin plot.

gaps.where: C2, C10 - reference genome and gene annotation
gaps.missing: The reference assembly is named ('HanXRQr2.0-SUNRISE') but no source URL, release date or checksum is given. The gene annotation used to assign 1,919 domestication-sweep genes and 2,062 improvement-sweep genes, and to classify them into functional categories (kernel oil biosynthesis, flowering time, ion transport, stress response), is not named at all - neither the GFF release nor the functional-annotation database or the assignment rule.
gaps.how_to_close: Cite the exact assembly and annotation files by URL and release (with checksums), and describe the functional-category assignment procedure and its source database version.

gaps.missing: The germplasm is identified by source institution only: 'All accessions used in this experiment came from the United States Department of Agriculture, Agricultural Research Service (USDA-ARS), North Central Regional Introduction Station (NCRPIS) in Ames, Iowa, USA.' No PI accession numbers are listed for the 274 lines in the paper text, and the fungicide used to treat the seeds is unnamed. Recorded for completeness; wet-lab steps are OOS and do not affect S.
gaps.how_to_close: List the 274 NCRPIS PI numbers in a supplementary table and name the fungicide and its application rate.
